_meta.purpose: Section 8 Step 6 judgement fields deferred to Section 9: pattern_or_taint, structural_or_context_heavy (stored as context_complexity in metadata), semgrep_representability (design doc Section 7.3).
_meta.rater: Single rater (Claude Code), judged from the hands-on construction of each case's Section 9 bundle. NOT independently double-rated; treat borderline supported/partially_supported calls as subject to review.

rubric.pattern_or_taint: pattern = a local syntactic/AST pattern flags the vulnerable instance; taint = a value must be tracked from an untrusted source to a sink across statements.
rubric.structural_or_context_heavy: structural = self-contained within a few lines; context_heavy = needs broader context (sibling methods/routes, framework or protocol semantics, what 'correct' looks like elsewhere) to tell the vulnerable instance from a look-alike.
rubric.supported: The vulnerable code has a matchable shape inside the function itself (dangerous call/API, missing-check or missing-annotation idiom, tainted flow to a sink, hard-coded secret/literal, missing entry in a literal security list).
rubric.partially_supported: Semgrep can observe part of the mechanism but important context is unavailable: a locally matchable faulty expression/statement-order whose wrongness is semantic (wrong operand/constant/argument, inverted comparison), or the sink/source/semantics lie outside the function, or framework/runtime behaviour decides harm.
rubric.unsupported: The vulnerable/patched difference is not a code-shape property: timing side channels, cryptographic parameter quality, data remanence, log volume, file-system/runtime behaviour, parser differentials, cross-function bookkeeping or business/authorization logic spread over statements.

_meta.near_duplicates_resolved: CASE-0277 and CASE-0338 retired (duplicates of CASE-0276 / CASE-0337); replaced by CASE-0341 and CASE-0342. See Implementation_Log.md Section 12.19.
